key: And the LORD came, and stood, and called as at other times: ‘Samuel, Samuel.’ Then Samuel said: ‘Speak; for Thy servant heareth.’
s: Called a fourth time in the night, the boy answers as Eli taught him, but without the name of the LORD; Rashi, on 3:10, takes the omission as caution, lest the voice be another’s, and Radak, on 3:10, as awe, still fearing to speak the Name in a prophetic vision.

evidence.gloss: [Rashi on 3:10, ‘And Samuel said: Speak’:] He did not mention the name of the Omnipresent as Eli had commanded him; he said, perhaps it is another voice … [Radak on 3:10, ‘Speak; for Thy servant heareth’:] He did not say ‘LORD’ as Eli had told him, for he was still afraid to mention the Name in the vision of prophecy.

reason: verse.js ok, ref 1 Samuel 3:10 and at [234,10] match. Plain sense faithful: the LORD calls at 3:4, 3:6, 3:8 and now a fourth time at 3:10; Eli had told him to answer ‘Speak, LORD’ (3:9) and the boy says only ‘Speak’; no four-word run from the key verse. Read the chapter 3 packet (Rashi, Radak, Metzudat David; no Midrash Rabbah on 1 Samuel). Rashi on ויאמר שמואל דבר: he did not mention the Name as Eli commanded, saying perhaps it is another voice. Radak on דבר כי שומע עבדך: he did not say the Name because he was still afraid to mention it in the prophetic vision (Radak then cites a derash that he feared a demon’s voice and calls it far-fetched; the sentence does not report or resolve that). The two readings genuinely differ and are named without resolution; ‘awe’ renders ירא within its range. Both evidence pieces machine-found in the packet. entry-check ok.
